summary: Market sentiment is cautiously mixed, with geopolitical tension in the Middle East dominating risk appetite as the Iran conflict continues to disrupt regional aviation, restrict Iranian flights across Iraqi airspace, and draw in major powers including Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and the UAE, while Trump's reported conversation with Xi Jinping about the war signals high-level diplomatic engagement but limited resolution. On the macro front, the 10-year Treasury yield hitting a 19-year high is reinforcing expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes, pressuring equities broadly while attracting contrarian bond buyers who see long-term value at elevated yields. In notable market movements, a pharma stock surged 150% on an injectables deal with Novo Nordisk, UAE markets declined on regional air travel warnings, gold is on pace for a weekly loss amid rising rate expectations, and oil prices dropped roughly 3% as the U.S. and Iran explore a diplomatic off-ramp despite Hormuz crude flows holding at 33.7 million barrels this week. The primary risk factors investors are monitoring include Hormuz strait disruption threatening global energy supply chains, escalating Saudi-Houthi military posturing, sticky inflation keeping the Fed hawkish, and political uncertainty as Senate Republicans scramble to reposition ahead of midterms. The short-term outlook remains volatile and headline-driven, with oil, bonds, and defense-linked assets most sensitive to any developments in the Iran conflict, while equity markets will likely trade defensively until clearer signals emerge on both the geopolitical and monetary policy fronts.
